entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

The table moves, but only a little. It shudders an inch on the flagstones and the oak groans against the iron ring at your wrists. The lamp rocks on the desk, the pen rolls, and the ledger slides a hand's breadth toward the edge. Your arms have nothing left in them. Your roar of *HOME* fills the beams, and for one breath every spear in the room swings your way.

Tessa is quicker than any of them. The ledger slides, and she has it in both hands and is on her knees before anyone can turn. She goes for the stove in the corner. The grey-eyed guard at her back doesn't need to think. His sword takes her across the ribs as she leaves his reach, and she drops with the book skidding out of her arms across the floor.

Then the Foreman's small, patient voice cuts across the room. "Alive. Both of them." A Tally-sworn blade comes down on you, flat-sided, and the dark closes like a door.

It is a little after one in the morning, and you wake to a dull, spreading ache. Your wrists are chained to a wall ring now, not a table, and the table has been righted and stands bolted to the floor. The stove still ticks. The ledger lies closed in the Foreman's hands, with the lamp set far out of anyone's reach. Tessa is unconscious on the pallet beside Gorrak, her ribs wrapped in a clean strip of linen. She is alive, and her hands are bound in front of her. Gorrak lies with his face turned to the wall. His bound hands have gone still.

The Foreman has not gone to bed. He sits with his bandaged side propped on a cushion, and the brass beads click. "You are not a stupid man, Emberhide," he says, so mildly that it is almost kind. "But you are a loud one, and I have learned what that means. Terms made at a table, with your hands near the lamp, are a mistake I will not make twice. The clause I struck is back in, and a second one besides. Your sister's life is the surety now, not the captain's. She will sit in a cell until you have served, and a rider leaves for the Border Stones at dawn whether you sign or not, unless you sign. You may take until the bell."

You have 1 hit point, no rage, no breath, and nothing that is yours. Six Tally-sworn stand along the walls. One of them is breathing through a bandage, and the ledger is in the Foreman's lap.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

You roar "HOME!" and heave. The table lifts a hand's breadth, and the chain bites your wrists. Then the weight of the oak beats the last of your strength and the table crashes back. The pen jumps, the ink pot spins, and the Foreman puts a steadying hand on the lamp.

Tessa doesn't wait to see you fail. She is across the tilted desk in one scrambled leap, snatching the lamp out from under his fingers, and she smashes it down on the open ledger. Oil spreads over the page and the flame catches in a bright sheet. For one heartbeat you see your own name burning in a clerk's neat hand.

The Foreman is faster than he looks. He drags the book clear by its cover and smothers the fire in his leather apron, hissing as the oil burns his palms. When he lifts the cloth, the book is black along one edge, with the first pages curled to ash, but it still opens.

Then the room closes on you. A longsword sweeps at your head and misses. The grey-eyed Tally-sworn behind Tessa cuts her down in mid-turn, and she drops across the table leg without a sound. The next blow comes in on your chained side, and you feel nothing at all.

You come to in the dark of the ledger-house some time before midnight. The stove has burned low, and the smell of burnt oil and singed paper hangs in the air. You are at 1 hit point, with your wrists chained to the table leg again and a fresh cord around your ankles. Tessa lies bound a pace from you with her hood over her face. You can see her chest rise and fall, and she doesn't stir. Gorrak is still on his pallet, and his eye is shut.

The Foreman sits at the desk with both palms wrapped in white linen and the scorched ledger open before him. He is writing slowly and awkwardly, with the pen in his fist. The beads lie on the page beside his hand, still. He doesn't look up.

"The terms are withdrawn," he says quietly. "Your sister stays in my ledger until you have served your first year and your second. Both of them. Her mule I will sell." The pen scratches. "Do you know what I regret, Emberhide? I would have been fair to you."

Six spears stand along the walls, and the singed guard is smiling.

entries.text: notebook: updated Break the Foreman's Ledger

The table goes over with a crash that shakes dust from the beams. The lamp bursts on the flagstones and the oil runs fire across the floor. The open ledger lands in it, and the flames take the old paper as if they'd been waiting. The Foreman throws himself backward out of his chair, and the fire misses him by a hand.

Then the grey-eyed guard's sword comes down flat across her temple, and she folds against the table leg and lies still. She is breathing, and you can see it. Your own guard, the one with the singed beard, swings at you and misses by a finger, and his blade rings off the ring in the floor.

Three of the Tally-sworn beat at the burning book with their cloaks and fail. The fourth gets his cloak over it and smothers what is left. The Foreman goes down on his knees in the smoke and lifts the thing out of the ash. Most of it is gone: the spine, the first leaves, the neat columns of numbers, all curling black. What he holds is a charred stub with a few pages hanging by their stitching. His soft hands are shaking, and when he looks up the mildness is gone from his face. "Kill him," he says, quite quietly. "No. Hold him. I will do it myself."

You are chained to a toppled table at 1 hit point. Five spears are closing in, Tessa is out cold at your knee, and Gorrak is struggling against his cords on the pallet, his burned face turned to the stove. It is your turn, and the stub of the ledger is two paces from your chain.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

You go up slowly, dragging your feet, and your eyes work while your legs don't. Six grey cloaks: two ahead, two at your elbows, two behind with the sergeant. The walk along the gate-top is narrow, with a drop on the left to the yard and the wall on the right. The ledger-house has one barred door facing the walk and one shuttered window on its east side, over the sluice drop. Far along the roof to the west you can make out the low hump of the wash-house. All the grey cloaks carry short swords and crossbows. None of them watch the sky or the drop. They watch you.

At the door you plant your heels and say it loud and flat. You'll hear his terms, but you'll see Tessa alive and whole first.

The sergeant doesn't even answer. A hand shoves you through the door, and it closes behind you.

The room is warmer than before and smells of tin, camphor and blood. The scorched floor has been scrubbed, the table righted, and the stove stoked. The Foreman sits behind the desk with a fresh bandage under his apron and a basin of reddened water at his elbow. The ledger lies before him in a new iron-bound chest with its lid propped open, its edges brown and brittle, and he has laid a clean cloth over it. The brass beads are in his hand.

"Whole," he says mildly. "You'll forgive me if I don't parade her. She is behind that door, and she is sleeping, because I wished her to. My mender has been busy and has earned it." He nods at an inner door, shut, with a bar across it. "You may see her when you have sworn. I thought we had agreed about the order of things."

Two grey cloaks stand behind you and the sergeant by the outer door. The Foreman's face shows exhaustion under the calm, and a little of the fastidious smile has gone. The beads click once.

"Let us not repeat ourselves. You read the terms and you struck a clause. I have struck another, since you were so kind as to call the captain's line into question. The terms stand. input.add_to_description: Day 21 ~3:05 AM: received Korvash in the ledger-house again with six grey cloaks; agreed to show Tessa alive before terms. The scorched ledger lies in a new iron chest by his chair. Tessa, bandaged, is on a stool by the stove with a grey cloak behind her, sewing a wound in his side.

entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

You drag your feet and try to read the walk as you go, but the wind is in your eyes, the torches gutter, and the cold has got into your head. You count cloaks and lose the count. You couldn't say which door holds the bar, or whether the windows are shuttered. You have the sense of a narrow walk with a drop on one side and little else.

At the ledger-house door you plant your heels. Your flat, carrying voice says you'll hear his terms, but you'll see Tessa alive and whole first. The sergeant starts to cuff you forward. Then a mild voice inside says, "Let him in. He is quite right to ask."

The room has been tidied. The table is righted, the scorch scrubbed to a grey smear, and the dead guard is gone. The Foreman sits in his chair with his shirt open and a fresh seam of stitches across his ribs, neat as a clerk's hand. Tessa sits on a stool at his side, bandaged at the skull, with a needle and thread in her fingers and a grey cloak behind her. Her eyes find yours. She is pale, but she is whole. The new iron-bound chest stands beside the Foreman's chair, and the scorched ledger lies on the desk with the cover shut and his hand on it.

"There," the Foreman says. "Alive, whole, and useful. She has a gentle hand, your sister. I should be sorry to lose it." The beads click. "Now we may talk like sensible people. Sit him down."

They sit you on the floor with your back to the table leg, and your hands are wired to it once more. The sergeant stands at your shoulder with five cloaks along the wall. The bar is down on the door behind you. Out in the dark a bell tolls the half hour, and the dawn bell is still some hours away.

"I will be brief," the Foreman says. "You have cost me a guard, a captain's loyalty, and a night's sleep. The terms stand as they were, with one addition. You will say the oath now, and you will say it of your own will, and your sister will mend the men you have hurt." He lifts the pen. "I have been patient. I have little left."

Tessa's needle has stopped. She is watching you, and her left hand lies flat on her knee, palm down and steady, the clan's sign for *wait*.

You are at 1 hit point, wired at the wrist, with the Foreman's eyes on you. What does Korvash say or do?
